bundles.title: Platform overview
bundles.intro: What Next Commerce is, how the two documentation sites divide the material, the Admin API versions, how to test safely, and the legacy identifiers an agent must not "correct". Start here before fetching a domain bundle.

bundles.title: Admin API
bundles.intro: The REST Admin API and its guides: orders and external checkout, subscriptions, fulfillment, and exports. Operations are listed by tag; the versioned OpenAPI file is the contract.

bundles.title: Payments and gateways
bundles.intro: Gateways, payment methods, gateway selection on API-created orders, disputes, and the Test Gateway. NEXT Payments processing rates are not published.

bundles.title: Campaigns
bundles.intro: Campaign funnels: the Campaigns API, Campaign Page Kit, starter templates, and the Admin API surface for campaigns and offers. Campaign orders are store orders.

bundles.title: Storefront
bundles.intro: Storefront themes and Theme Kit, template objects, tags and filters, theme settings, the storefront GraphQL API, checkout links, and event tracking.

bundles.title: Apps and webhooks
bundles.intro: Building apps with OAuth, app manifests and settings, service integrations (fulfillment, disputes, attribution), and every webhook event with its payload.

capabilities.title: Admin API
capabilities.summary: The REST Admin API manages store resources: products, orders, customers, subscriptions, fulfillment, payments, campaigns, and more. Access is by OAuth app token against https://{store}.29next.store/api/admin/, with the version selected per request by the X-29next-API-Version header. 2024-04-01 is the stable version; 2023-02-10 is deprecated; unstable carries in-progress changes.

api_operations.summary: Retrieve general business information and store settings.
Retrieve the download URL for a completed export file.
Retrieve a list of metadata definitions.
Partial update an existing metadata definition.

notes: The developer portal has no changelog of its own; version history is on the merchant changelog.
There is no consolidated migration guide between API versions yet.

capabilities.title: Orders and external checkout
capabilities.summary: Orders can be created through the Admin API from an external checkout (cart, order, upsell flow) and managed afterwards: fulfil, refund, capture, cancel, and edit. Campaign and storefront orders land in the same orders list.

capabilities.title: Subscriptions
capabilities.summary: Native recurring orders. Merchants configure phases, statuses, pause, cancellation paths, decline salvage, and account updater in the dashboard; developers create and manage subscriptions through the Admin API. Renewals are not a separate webhook: a renewal surfaces as transaction.created (and order.created) with billing_cycle set.

api_operations.summary: Delete a subscription line in an existing subscription line.
Trigger a renewal payment retry for a subscription.
Retrieve a list of transactions in an existing subscription.

notes: There is no subscription.renewed event. Detect renewals from transaction.created with billing_cycle.

capabilities.title: Payments and gateways
capabilities.summary: Merchants add bankcard gateways and alternative payment methods under Settings > Payments and group them for routing and failure cascading. Developers choose a gateway on an API-created order with payment_details.payment_gateway or payment_gateway_group, and integrate each payment method through its guide. NEXT Payments is the platform's own processing service.

Resolve a dispute with a resolution and optional external refund.
Retrieve a list of gatway groups.

notes: NEXT Payments processing rates are not published in the documentation; they are quoted by sales.

capabilities.title: Disputes
capabilities.summary: Disputes are chargebacks. Merchants review and respond to them in the dashboard and report on them; apps can act as a dispute service and receive dispute events.

capabilities.title: Fulfillment
capabilities.summary: Orders are fulfilled through locations, fulfillment statuses, and location-based routing. Apps can register as a fulfillment service and receive assigned fulfillment orders through the Admin API.

capabilities.title: Campaigns
capabilities.summary: Campaigns are custom checkout funnels (landing, checkout, upsell, receipt pages) backed by the CORS-enabled Campaigns API, built with the Campaign Page Kit and starter templates. A campaign's checkout is separate from the storefront checkout, but its orders are ordinary store orders that share the orders list, inventory, and subscriptions.

capabilities.title: Storefront themes
capabilities.summary: The hosted storefront is rendered from a theme built with Django Template Language. Merchants install and customise themes under Storefront > Themes; developers build themes locally with Theme Kit (the ntk CLI: ntk pull, ntk push, ntk watch), starting from the Spark starter theme, and query storefront data through the GraphQL API.

capabilities.title: Checkout links
capabilities.summary: Prebuilt URLs that open the storefront checkout with products, quantities, and attribution already applied, for use from ads, emails, and campaign pages.

capabilities.title: Apps and OAuth
capabilities.summary: Apps extend a store through OAuth, a manifest, settings, snippets, and storefront extensions, and can act as fulfillment, dispute, or marketing-attribution services. Merchants install apps from the dashboard; App Kit is the developer toolchain.

api_operations.summary: Retrieve a object of all app settings.
Partially update an existing app settings.

notes: The merchant site documents individual apps (Klaviyo, ShipStation, Gorgias, and others) under /docs/apps/<app>, not app installation in general.

capabilities.title: Webhooks
capabilities.summary: Stores send signed JSON webhooks for events on orders, customers, subscriptions, transactions, disputes, fulfillment, products, gateways, tickets, exports, apps, and the store itself. Merchants configure endpoints in the dashboard; developers manage them through the Admin API and verify the X-29Next-Signature header.

capabilities.title: Testing and test orders
capabilities.summary: There is no separate sandbox. Test cards (6011111111111117, and 6011000990139424 for 3DS) create tagged Test Orders on live stores without touching a gateway; the Test Gateway produces realistic test transactions when an integration needs them.
notes: Do not tell a prospect there is no test mode; test cards work on live stores.

capabilities.title: Legacy identifiers (29next)
capabilities.summary: Next Commerce was formerly 29 Next, and the platform still carries that name in its core technical identifiers: store and account hostnames ({store}.29next.store, accounts.29next.com), the X-29next-API-Version and X-29Next-Signature headers, and the API key namespace. These are current, in use on every store, and not scheduled to change. Use them exactly as written.
notes: Never rewrite 29next identifiers to nextcommerce; the requests would fail.

capabilities.title: AI agent skills
capabilities.summary: Pre-built skills that give AI coding agents platform knowledge (theme development, campaign setup, bulk operations, daily ops scans), installable with the skills CLI or loadable as plain markdown.
